[ASSISTANT_SAID] The exact mechanisms of priming are not well understood, and different researchers have proposed different theories.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Priming involves the idea that exposure to certain stimuli can activate related concepts or associations in the brain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of priming is that if shown a picture of a tree, the concept of "tree" might become more active in the brain, influencing the identification of an ambiguous image as a tree.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] One possible explanation for priming is that it involves changes in the strength of connections between different neurons in the brain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Increased activity of certain neurons due to exposure to a stimulus may strengthen the connections between these neurons and others.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Another possibility is that priming involves changes in the level of neurotransmitters, such as dopamine, in the brain.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] More research is needed to fully understand the underlying mechanisms of priming.
